beats.text: In Armenia, 83.9% of health spending comes from private sources. In East Timor, just 7%.
Armenia is the world's highest. It counts funds from households, corporations, and non-profits paid directly or via insurance.
Myanmar at 82.8%, Bangladesh at 82%, Nigeria at 74.4%, and Syria at 73.3% follow close behind.
The USA is 46%, while China sits at 42.9%.
India is 58.6%, which is 8.4 times East Timor.
In Japan, private sources fund only 15.2% of health care.
Who pays for healthcare in your country?
